newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts say ING shares look overvalued.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say ING shares look overvalued.

text.p: The sharp rise in the price of ING Groep NV in the wake of its latest takeover prompted some brokers to declare the shares overvalued on Wednesday.
Two analysts downgraded their recommendations on the Dutch financial services group while another considered the price had risen too quickly, although some brokers remained bullish.
ING announced on Tuesday it had agreed to buy U.S. insurer Equitable of Iowa Companies for $2.2 billion in shares and cash plus the assumption of $400 million of debt.
The shares were trading at 105.10 guilders at 1315 GMT, up 10 percent in two days and 69 percent so far in 1997.
CS First Boston cut its ING recommendation to 'hold' from 'buy,' with analyst Kishore Banger saying the stock had passed his valuation target of 100 guilders and appeared fully valued.
Kempen and Co analyst Hans Pluijgers lowered his ING rating to Market Performer from Outperformer over 12 months.
He said although Equitable of Iowa was a good fit with ING for the long term, he was disappointed it would add only one percent to earnings per share in 1998.
He also based his downgrading on the fact that ING shares had outperfored the Dutch sharemarket, which has risen 44 percent this year, and ING's high price earnings multiple.
Pluijgers puts ING on 18 times forecast 1998 EPS, compared with 17.5 for rival Dutch insurer Aegon which, he argues, should command a higher multiple.

Andrew Goodwin of UBS considered ING shares no more than a Hold for investors with an outlook of three to six months, saying the takeover was not as beneficial as the price rise suggested. "In the short term, the share price has probably gone a bit too far," he said, adding however that the shares had good potential for the longer term.
Paribas analyst Tom Bennett said it was tempting to consider a downgrade as the price reaction was "nonsense".
"However, ING is still within my Buy range," he added.
Bennett said ING shares could rise another eight percent, assuming no change in the overall Dutch sharemarket, before he would consider changing his recommendation.
He said ING was trading at 22 times his forecast of 1997 earnings, putting it in line with the Dutch market. "But the Dutch market isn't growing at the same rate," he said.
Generale Bank said in a research note that the takeover strengthened its view that ING's fair value was 140 guilders.
